name: Question 12
worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set is the number of elements contained within it. A set is infinite if it has infinitely many elements.

- The set $A$ is finite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{(0)}(x) & ={e}^{-x} \\ {f}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{-x})=-{e}^{-x} \\ {f}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-{e}^{-x})={e}^{-x} \\ {f}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{-x})=-{e}^{-x} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $A$ contains only two elements:

$$
A={{e}^{-x},-{e}^{-x}}
$$

Consequently, $|A|=2,$ which is finite.

- The set $B$ is infinite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{(0)}(x) & ={e}^{3x} \\ {g}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{3x})=3{e}^{3x} \\ {g}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{e}^{3x})=9{e}^{3x} \\ {g}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(9{e}^{3x})=27{e}^{3x} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we can write our set as follows:

$$
B={{e}^{3x},3{e}^{3x},9{e}^{3x},27{e}^{3x},…}
$$

Consequently, $B$ is infinite.

- The set $C$ is finite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{(0)}(x) & ={e}^{x+1} \\ {h}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x+1})={e}^{x+1} \\ {h}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x+1})={e}^{x+1} \\ {h}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x+1})={e}^{x+1} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $C$ contains only one element:

$$
C={{e}^{x+1}}
$$

Consequently, $|C|=1,$ which is finite.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only."

html:
Question 12
?

Which of the following sets are infinite?

  1. A={f(n)(x)=dndxn(e−x):n∈N0}
  2. B={g(n)(x)=dndxn(e3x):n∈N0}
  3. C={h(n)(x)=dndxn(ex+1):n∈N0}
a
A and C only
b
A and B only
c
None of the sets are infinite.
d
C only
e
B only
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The cardinality of a finite set is the number of elements contained within it. A set is infinite if it has infinitely many elements.

  • The set A is finite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following: f(0)(x)=e−xf(1)(x)=ddx(e−x)=−e−xf(2)(x)=ddx(−e−x)=e−xf(3)(x)=ddx(e−x)=−e−x⋮ Thus, A contains only two elements: A={e−x,−e−x} Consequently, |A|=2, which is finite.

  • The set B is infinite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following: g(0)(x)=e3xg(1)(x)=ddx(e3x)=3e3xg(2)(x)=ddx(3e3x)=9e3xg(3)(x)=ddx(9e3x)=27e3x⋮ Thus, we can write our set as follows: B={e3x,3e3x,9e3x,27e3x,…} Consequently, B is infinite.

  • The set C is finite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following: h(0)(x)=ex+1h(1)(x)=ddx(ex+1)=ex+1h(2)(x)=ddx(ex+1)=ex+1h(3)(x)=ddx(ex+1)=ex+1⋮ Thus, C contains only one element: C={ex+1} Consequently, |C|=1, which is finite.

Therefore, the correct answer is "B only."
